Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.
Rejoinder affidavit filed today on behalf of the applicant is taken on record.
2.  Sri Suresh Bahadur Singh, learned AGA for the State apprised the Court that on 08.03.2022 notice has been served upon the informant.
Despite service of notice, none appeared on behalf of the informant.

3. Heard Sri Ashutosh, Advocate holding brief of Sri Pavan Kumar, learned counsel for the applicant and Sri Suresh Bahadur Singh, learned AGA for the State.
4. The instant bail application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No. 66 of 2021, under Sections 363, 366, 506, 302, 201, 376(2)n IPC and Section 3, 4 POCSO Act,
Police Station Nawabganj, District Bareilly during pendency of the trial.

sentences.text: FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and another on 14.02.2021 and according to the FIR on 09.02.2021 daughter of the informant aged about 12 years had gone along with her mother but thereafter did not return and after search informant came to know that she along with her also taken Rs. 20,000/- and golden earrings.

It is further mentioned in the FIR that from the call details from SIM of the daughter of the informant, it was revealed that she was in touch of the applicant and when informant made query from the applicant then he refused to provide whereabouts of his daughter.
It is further mentioned in the FIR that informant is having doubt that applicant has enticed his minor daughter and some incident has been happened with her.

6. Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that from the perusal of the FIR, it appears that on the basis of suspicion applicant has been made accused in the present matter and as applicant had already made accused in the FIR, therefore, police arrested him and as per allegation applicant confessed his guilt and on his pointing out the dead body of the deceased was recovered from sugarcane filed.

7. He further submits that on the basis of totally false allegation applicant has been made accused in the present matter and applicant neither confessed his guilt nor the dead body of the deceased was recovered on his pointing out.

He further submits that except the fact that applicant made conversation with the deceased before the incident there is no cogent evidence against the applicant on record and it appears that after recovery of dead body on the basis of totally false allegation applicant has been made accused in the present matter by showing that the dead body was recovered on his pointing out.
8. He next submits that applicant is not having any criminal history and in the present matter he is in jail since 15.02.2021 i.e. for more than two and half years.

He further submits that in the charge-sheet there are as many as 19 prosecution witnesses but till date only two prosecution witnesses could be examined, therefore, there is no hope of early disposal of the trial, therefore,
considering the facts and circumstances of the case, applicant should be enlarged on bail.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that deceased was hardly 12 years old girl and from perusal of the call details of the victim i.e. deceased and applicant, it appears that both made conversation just before the incident and on the pointing out of the applicant the dead body of the deceased was recovered.
Learned AGA further pointed out that there is allegation that he firstly committed rape with the deceased and thereafter strangulated her.

Learned AGA further submits that as per FSL report, rape was committed with the deceased.
10.
I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

11. Although, it is a case of circumstantial evidence and applicant in the present matter is in jail for last about two and half years but it is a case, in which, a 12 year minor girl was firstly raped and thereafter was strangulated.

12. From the record, it further reflects that before alleged incident applicant made conversation with the deceased and thereafter deceased was eloped and her dead body was found in the sugarcane Vikas Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185014582/
2 field on the pointing out of the applicant.

sentences.text:
13. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicant is not entitled to be released on bail.
14. Accordingly, the instant bail application is rejected.

15. However, considering the fact that applicant is in jail for almost two and half years, trial court is directed to conclude the trial of the case within a period of eight months from the date of production of certified copy of this order strictly as per provision of Section 309 Cr.P.C. as well as Section 35 of POCSO Act, if there is no legal impediment.

16. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.

Order Date :- 19.9.2023 AK Pandey  Vikas Kumar vs State Of U.P. And 3 Others on 19 September, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/185014582/
